subject: Materials Science
title: Zinc Oxide Nanostructures
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Zinc Oxide Nanostructures.

hook.text: ZnO grows into nanowires, nanobelts, and nanoflowers — the most morphologically diverse nanomaterial known.

buildup.text: ZnO is a wide band gap semiconductor (3.37 eV) — it emits UV light, is piezoelectric, and is transparent when thin.

discovery.text: ZnO nanowire arrays generate electricity from vibrations — nanogenerators that could power wearable devices.

twist.text: ZnO dissolves in acidic and basic conditions — limiting its use in harsh environments despite its versatile properties.

climax.text: ZnO nanoparticles are in sunscreens, rubber, paint, and electronics — one of the most produced nanomaterials globally.

punchline.text: ZnO senses, generates power, blocks UV, and glows — it does it all at nanoscale.

quiz.question: What unique property do ZnO nanowire arrays have?
options: They generate electricity from mechanical vibrations via the piezoelectric effect
